prior_scan_disposition.note: Scan-009 found 1 low-severity finding on src/pages/action/index.astro (Braver Angels self-description attribution). That file did not appear in the current diff. The two files in this scan (blog posts) received URL and fair-witness hedge fixes that appear to remediate issues from earlier scans or internal review.

findings.description: UDHR abbreviation appears on first body-text use (line 82) without expansion. The glossary page defines it, but inline first-use expansion assists readers — especially the voter lens (8th-grade reading level) who may not navigate to the glossary. The abbreviation also appears unexpanded in the politician lensFraming (frontmatter line 36).
findings.suggestion: Expand on first body use: 'The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) encodes this principle...' The frontmatter lensFraming for politician could similarly expand it.
findings.context: The UDHR encodes this principle in Articles 1 and 21: equal dignity and democratic participation as structural requirements, not aspirational ideals (UN General Assembly, 1948).

findings.description: Parenthetical '(though it does)' asserts that regulatory capture has occurred as editorial fact, without citation or hedging. The surrounding sentence carefully distinguishes structural incentive from capture — the parenthetical undercuts that careful framing by asserting the stronger claim without evidence.
findings.suggestion: Remove the parenthetical or hedge it: '(though evidence of such capture exists — see e.g., [citation])' or simply delete '(though it does)' since the structural argument holds without it.
findings.context: governance proposals get crafted to accommodate their interests — not because regulatory capture has occurred (though it does) but because the structural asymmetry reshapes what proposals appear viable.

findings.description: Five E-prime violations in the body text: 'is a framing choice' (line 73), 'is illustrative, not evidential' (line 109), 'were not neutral records' (line 117), 'may be inflated' (line 31), 'would have been inflated' (line 57). The site glossary declares all user-facing copy follows E-prime. The why-war post achieves near-complete E-prime compliance; this post has not received the same editorial pass.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite each instance with active verbs. Examples: 'is a framing choice' -> 'represents a framing choice'; 'is illustrative, not evidential' -> 'serves as illustration, not evidence'; 'were not neutral records' -> 'carried design decisions, priorities, and reasoning patterns' (which the sentence already says); 'may be inflated' -> 'may overstate the score'; 'would have been inflated' -> 'would have overstated the drift'.
findings.context: Whether this constitutes a "tool becoming a peer" is a framing choice — the underlying dynamic is context accumulation through documentation absorption.

findings.description: Claim 'This happens more often than developers admit' presents an inference about developer behavior as observation. No survey data, citation, or hedging supports the claim. Fair witness standard calls for distinguishing direct observation from inference.
findings.suggestion: Hedge the claim: 'This may happen more often than developers realize' or 'In our experience, this happens frequently' — or cite a source if one exists.
findings.context: This happens more often than developers admit. When working inside an LLM-assisted coding session, the conversation *feels* like the record.

epistemic_flags: E-prime violations in blog posts carry lower severity than in site pages — blog voice permits slightly looser register, though the glossary commits to E-prime site-wide
The why-war post achieves remarkably clean E-prime compliance for a 248-line analytical essay — only one 'are' instance, inside a direct UDHR quote
Both diffs in this scan range appear to remediate prior quality issues (URL fix, fair-witness hedge), suggesting the feedback loop operates effectively
